title: Part D: Structure, Formularies, and the IRA Drug Reforms
summary: Medicare Part D is the voluntary outpatient prescription drug benefit, delivered by private plans and subsidized by the federal government. The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 made the most significant Part D reforms since the benefit was created — including direct Medicare drug price negotiation and a $2,000 out-of-pocket cap.

objectives.text: Explain the structure of Part D coverage including formularies and cost-sharing tiers
Describe what the Inflation Reduction Act changed about Part D
Explain how the Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program works

content_blocks.body: Medicare Part D was created by the Medicare Modernization Act (MMA) of 2003 and became effective in January 2006. It introduced voluntary prescription drug coverage to Medicare for the first time — an enormous policy change that affected virtually every Medicare beneficiary.

**Voluntary participation.** Medicare beneficiaries can enroll in a stand-alone Prescription Drug Plan (PDP) for traditional Medicare or receive Part D as part of Medicare Advantage (MA-PD). Beneficiaries who go without creditable drug coverage for 63+ days face late enrollment penalties.

**Formularies.** Each Part D plan maintains a formulary — a list of covered drugs organized into tiers, typically:
- Tier 1: Preferred generics (lowest cost-sharing)
- Tier 2: Non-preferred generics
- Tier 3: Preferred brand-name drugs
- Tier 4: Non-preferred brand-name drugs
- Tier 5: Specialty drugs (highest cost-sharing)

Formularies must cover at least two drugs in every drug category/class and all drugs in six 'protected' classes: antidepressants, antipsychotics, anticonvulsants, immunosuppressants, antiretrovirals, and antineoplastics.

The IRA made transformational changes to Part D:

**$2,000 out-of-pocket cap.** Beginning in 2025, Medicare beneficiaries face a $2,000 annual cap on out-of-pocket prescription drug costs — eliminating the 'catastrophic' phase where patients previously had unlimited cost exposure.

**Insulin cap.** Insulin costs capped at $35/month for Part D enrollees (effective 2023).

**Vaccines.** All ACIP-recommended vaccines covered at $0 cost-sharing.

**Drug price negotiation.** For the first time in Medicare's history, CMS is authorized to negotiate prices directly with pharmaceutical manufacturers for selected high-expenditure drugs. The first 10 drugs were selected in 2023; negotiated prices take effect in 2026. CMS has authority to expand to 20+ drugs annually.

The IRA drug reforms represent the largest change to Part D since its creation and are expected to generate $98 billion in net Medicare savings over 10 years.
